moments.title: The busiest sky
moments.why: 16 simultaneous downlinks, the most in the archive. Every voice of the choir has something to sing.

moments.title: The quietest sky
moments.why: 1 downlink. The choir thins to almost nothing, which is what a quiet network actually sounds like.

moments.title: The faintest voice
moments.why: EURC at -200 dBm, the weakest power the network is recorded receiving more than once (13 times across the archive). Received power sets how loudly a voice sings, so this one is a whisper.

moments.title: The loudest torrent
moments.why: TESS downlinking at 125.1 Mb/s. Data rate chooses the voice part, and nothing else in the archive sings this high.

moments.title: One craft, two voices
moments.why: KPLO holding 2 downlinks at once (X-band at 8500 kb/s, S-band at 8 kb/s). Each carrier is scored independently, so one spacecraft can land in two voice parts simultaneously.

moments.title: All three complexes at once
moments.why: Goldstone, Madrid and Canberra all carrying traffic in the same moment. Each complex is panned to its own position, so the choir spreads across the whole stereo field.

moments.title: The rarest visitor: AGM1
moments.why: AGM1 appears in 110 of 129,210 recorded moments (0.09%). Most of the time it is simply not being listened to.

moments.title: Many at once
moments.why: 4 spacecraft acquired in the same moment (EMM, M01O, MRO, TGO). An acquisition cuts the phrase short and fires the cadence early.
